label: Bad and expensive Wine
name: Bad and expensive Wine
src_text_orig: Einige Tage ließ mich außm Duke of Richmond, einem sehr berühmten Wirthshauß der benachbarten Suffolkstreet, speisen, sehr theuer. Dort sowol als an vielen andern Orten sind 3 Tafeln. Die erste à 30 Pence, die andere à 22, und darnach die geringste. Man speiset gut, muß aber ehrenthalben Wein trinken, der in Engelland sehr theuer, nicht sowohl weil er in Frankreich oder Portugal wächßt, sondern weil aufm Gallon Portugesischen Wein 7, aufm französischen 14 Pence Umgelt liegt, wie dann mit Portugal solch ein Vergleich getroffen ist, daß die ZöIle deß französischen Weins immer gedoppelt vom portugesischen sein sollen. Daher der Champagne Wein biß 20 Sh., der Burgunder biß 5, der gemeine Bordeaux wein 2 ½, der schlechte Portugeser abet biß 1 ½ oder 2 Sh. kost. Welches um desto theurer zu halten, daß alle diese Weine nicht rein, sondern gekünstelt und gemischt sind.
src_text_translation: A few days I dined at the Duke of Richmond, a very famous inn in neighbouring Suffolk Street, very expensive. There, as in many other places, are 3 tables. The first at 30 pence, the other at 22, and then the cheapest. One dines well, but must drink wine for honour's sake, which is very expensive in England, not because it grows in France or Portugal, but because a gallon of Portuguese wine costs 7 pence and 14 pence a gallon of French wine, just as a settlement has been made with Portugal that the price of French wine should always be double that of Portuguese wine. Hence the Champagne wine costs up to 20 sh., the Burgundy wine up to 5, the common Bordeaux wine 2 ½, but the bad Portuguese wine up to 1 ½ or 2 sh. Which is all the more expensive, considering that all these wines are not pure, but artificial and mixed.
src_source:
Haller, Albrecht von. Albrecht Hallers Tagebücher seiner Reisen nach Deutschland, Holland und England, 1723-1727. Edited by Erich Hintzsche, Hans Huber, 1971, p. 88.

There are two manuscripts documenting Haller’s travels, N Haller 39 and N Haller 38. Both are located at the Burgerbibliothek Bern but have not been digitalized. N Haller 38 are his original notes in tiny handwriting, with barely any space, and many crossed out sections, making it very hard to read. N Haller 39 was written after the completion of his travels, based on his notes, but giving a much more detailed account. The editor, Erich Hintzsche, transcribed both of these versions: the notes (N Haller 38) are Albrecht Hallers Tagebuch seiner Studienreise nach London, Paris, Straßburg und Basel, 1727-1728, published in 1968, and the extended version (N Haller 39) is Albrecht Hallers Tagebücher seiner Reisen nach Deutschland, Holland und England, 1723-1727, published in 1971. We are quoting from both versions, so be aware which one is cited.

label: Turk's Head Coffee House
name: Turk's Head Coffee House
src_text_orig: War im Coffee-house Turkshead, wo sonderlich die Teutschen hinzukommen pflegen. Die Kaffehäuser sind der Zeitvertreib eines großen Theils von Engelland. Viele thun auf der Welt nichts, als aus einem ins andere seine Grillen hintragen. Hier liest man tausenderley Zeitangen, maßen alle Tage unterschiedliche zu London gedrukt werden, ohne die fremde. Über die darin enthaltnen Zufälle zanken sich die tiefsinnigen und spizfündigen Engelländer und reden so frey von denen Hofsachen, als wären sie zu Bern.
src_text_translation: Went to the Turkshead coffee-house, where the Germans in particular tend to come. Coffee-houses are the pastime of a large part of England. Many do nothing in the world but carry their whims from one to another. Here one reads a thousand and one tales of the times, all of which are printed differently every day in London, without foreign ones. The deep-minded and scatter-footed Englishmen quarrel about the coincidences contained therein and talk as freely about court matters as if they were in Bern.
